_comment: Execution Governance Layer (EGL) configuration. All constants here are EITHER domain-expert-required (Category C) OR engineering defaults requiring sensitivity analysis (Category B). See parameter_provenance.md §5 for justification of each value.

phase_boundaries_minutes._comment: Golden Hour boundary = 60 min (ICRC Trauma Care 2013; FEMA ICS operational period standard). Sustained Ops = up to 6 hours (FEMA ICS P-1035 operational period). These are literature-backed, not heuristic.

irreversibility_coefficients._comment: Category C — MUST be signed off by emergency management authority before operational deployment. Defaults are engineering estimates based on ICS resource commitment doctrine and UNDRR 2019 guidance on evacuation reversals. authorized_by must be populated.

SCOUT_REROUTE.basis: Negligible commitment: only a waypoint change, no fuel committed.

SCOUT_DISPATCH.basis: Low fuel spend, recallable within one tick (~1 min). Lower than rescue due to no passenger commitment.

RESCUE_DISPATCH.basis: FEMA ICS resource commitment doctrine: ground team committed for 30+ min, fuel + crew deployed.

HELICOPTER_AIRLIFT.basis: High fuel cost, mechanical wear per sortie, limited daily sortie count. Based on USCG SAR operational cost model.

EVACUATION_ORDER.basis: UNDRR 2019: mass population movement causes panic if reversed; logistical cascade effect.

regret_costs._comment: Category B — engineering defaults with literature basis. Sensitivity range documents what changes ±30% of these values.

C_route_closure.basis: Relative cost of losing a route vs acting on bad information (C_info_wrong=1.0 reference). Route closure is worse than bad intel because it is environment-imposed and cannot be corrected by better data alone.
C_route_closure.impact_of_30pct_change: Affects DEFER/EXECUTE boundary for route-uncertainty-dominant scenarios by ~8-12% of decisions.

C_golden_hour.basis: Cowley et al. (1971, J Trauma): survival probability approximately halves after 60 min for severe trauma. Golden hour loss is twice as costly as bad intelligence. Value 2.5 = 2.5× C_info_wrong.

theta_crisis.basis: ESCALATE threshold set equal to C_golden_hour. Rationale: if both regrets exceed the golden-hour cost, the situation is genuinely critical — no option is clearly better.

decision_margin._comment: Category B — base margin derived from control theory: 5% of max signal range prevents oscillation. Max R range ≈ 3.0, so 5% = 0.15. Minimum stable margin 0.03 = 1% of range.

base_margin.basis: Control theory minimum hysteresis: 5% of signal range [0, ~3.0]. Prevents flip-flop between EXECUTE and DEFER on consecutive ticks.

min_margin.basis: 1% of signal range. Below this, regrets are so close that ESCALATE is the correct decision regardless — oscillation risk is moot.

defer_escalation._comment: All three values derived from base_margin and golden_hour_end / timestep (60 min / 10 min avg re-eval = 6 ticks). Not independent constants.

defer_escalate_count.basis: floor(golden_hour_end / 10 min average re-evaluation) = floor(60/10) = 6. After a full golden-hour cycle of DEFERs, human review is mandatory.

defer_margin_decay_per_tick.basis: (base_margin - min_margin) / defer_escalate_count = (0.15 - 0.03) / 6 = 0.02. Fully derived — not an independent constant.
defer_margin_decay_per_tick.derivation: derived from base_margin, min_margin, and defer_escalate_count

access_equity._comment: Category B — AEM slope: isolated node (reachability=0) gets +30% urgency boost. Prevents systematic under-allocation to communities with no self-evacuation option.

aem_slope.basis: Engineering estimate. Sets maximum urgency boost for completely isolated nodes at 30% above baseline. Calibrate against regional equity metrics.
aem_slope.impact_of_30pct_change: Affects dispatch priority for low-reachability nodes by ±9-15% of urgency score.

source_diversity._comment: Category B — w_delta weight for source diversity index in epsilon. Allocates 15% of epistemic readiness score to source independence.

w_delta.basis: Set equal to geva_exploration_weight (0.05 base, boosted to 0.15) to maintain dimensional scale consistency across the system.

staged_dispatch._comment: Category B — agent commits to this fraction of route before re-evaluating for high-irreversibility actions (I >= 0.70).

staging_fraction.basis: Engineering estimate: 1/4 of route gives enough proximity for fresher sensor data while limiting fuel committed. Requires field validation.

irreversibility_threshold_for_staging.basis: Only stage evacuation orders (I=0.90) to prevent panic. Helicopters (I=0.75) are not staged as they ignore ground blockages and floods.

human_override._comment: Category C — MUST be set by incident commander per mission type. Operational range: 30s (fast-tempo) to 120s (deliberate). Defaults are starting points only.

GOLDEN_HOUR.basis: Tight timeout during golden hour — every 30s of inaction has measurable survival cost (Cowley 1971).

SUSTAINED_OPS.basis: Standard deliberate decision window for non-golden-hour dispatch.

RECOVERY.basis: Extended window during recovery phase — fatigue means slower cognition; more time reduces errors.

human_override._timeout_default_basis: Low-I actions (scouts) default EXECUTE on timeout — error is recoverable. High-I actions (rescue/evacuation) default DEFER — irreversible harm avoided. Threshold 0.50 splits scout-class from rescue-class.

ethical_profiles._comment: Category C — profile weights MUST be authorized by EMA authority before deployment. These encode value judgments about relative worth of crew vs. civilian lives.

CREW_CONSERVATIVE.basis: High-risk entry environments (chemical, structural collapse). Crew safety paramount.

BALANCED.basis: Standard multi-victim flood/earthquake operations. Default profile.

CIVILIAN_PRIORITY.basis: Mass casualty events where civilian survival probability degrades rapidly. Accepts higher crew risk.
